textRuns.value: Above a high threshold, fire sizes follow a generalised Pareto tail. Its shape says how slowly the chance of a bigger fire fades: at 1 or more the fitted mean is infinite, so no return level is published. An Anderson-Darling goodness-of-fit test flags the countries where the fitted law does not describe the episodes: it flags the two countries without a level, so their shape above 1 reads as a poor fit at this threshold, not as an established property of their fires. One more country is flagged and keeps its levels, to be read with caution. Each country is fitted on fire episodes above 500 ha, EFFIS, 2016 to 2025: fires within 3 days of each other count as one episode. Only EU27 countries with enough episodes are fitted. Levels stop at twice the observed period, so there is no 50-year figure. The shape depends on the threshold: pick Portugal and its shape falls below 1 at the 1 000 ha threshold. Click a country on the map or a row of the table to draw its curves.
